**Test image observations:** Mango leaf with necrotic tip (brown, dried-out tip area), some scattered brown lesions on the leaf surface, and general yellowing. The tip dieback is the dominant feature — the leaf tip is dead/brown and crispy-looking.

Now checking one reference per class:
Die_Back shows a fully desiccated, dead brown leaf. The test image has a mostly green leaf with tip necrosis. Let me check Anthracnose.
Powdery Mildew shows white/gray powdery coating on the leaf — not matching the test image. Checking Sooty Mould.

**Analysis:**

- **Sooty Mould**: Black/dark sooty spots covering the leaf surface — not present in test image.
- **Powdery Mildew**: White powdery coating — not present in test image.
- **Die_Back**: Fully desiccated, completely brown/dead leaf — more severe than test image.
- **Anthracnose**: Yellowed leaf with brown necrotic areas. The test image has a green leaf with brown tip necrosis and scattered lesions, which aligns more with Anthracnose (tip and margin necrosis are classic Anthracnose symptoms on mango leaves).

The test image shows a green leaf with distinct brown necrotic tip and scattered brown spots — this pattern (tip necrosis, discrete lesions) is consistent with Anthracnose rather than full Die_Back (which is complete desiccation), Sooty Mould (black sooty deposits), or Powdery Mildew (white powder).
